purpose: Resolve row-key semantics in the Palmer LTER adult-and-chick census before defining any colony-level reproductive-success model.
trigger: The earlier island-chick-success workflow failed on duplicate usable key ('LIT', '8.0', 1996) when keying rows only by island, colony_code, and season_start_year.
usable_row_rule: five Palmer islands; finite num_breeding_pairs > 0; parseable time and non-empty colony_code
outputs: number and identity of coarse duplicate keys
all non-outcome fields for each duplicate group
collision count under each candidate key
whether duplicate groups agree on adult breeding-pair counts
whether duplicate groups differ in study_name, time, or census_time
decision_boundary: Do not choose a deduplication rule until the non-outcome audit is recorded.
Do not inspect num_chicks to decide which duplicate row to retain.
If a finer documented non-outcome key uniquely separates rows, preserve those rows as distinct observations and redesign the reproductive-success unit accordingly.
If rows are exact duplicates on all non-outcome fields, a deterministic duplicate-collapse rule may be frozen before num_chicks is opened.
If duplicate semantics remain ambiguous after the non-outcome audit, colony-level chick-success inference remains blocked.
next_gate: After key semantics are resolved, freeze the colony-level chick-production model before retrieving or analyzing num_chicks.
